alignment.rationale: Both develop source evaluation, academic writing, research integrity, reflection and collaborative learning. UvA additionally introduces geographical academic practice and interview skills.

Both introduce research design, statistics, empirical data and survey/experimental reasoning. UvA combines this with introductory interviews and socio-spatial questions; UCR develops a full empirical project.

Both conduct supervised survey research, analyse original data and report findings. UvA also requires residential spatial fieldwork and thematic interview analysis; UCR centres psychological inclusion and leadership.

Both connect environmental pressures, infrastructure and institutions to changing places. UCR centres adaptation and water governance in Zeeland; UvA studies a wider range of Amsterdam urban dynamics, including housing and mobility.

Both analyse institutions, participation, conflict and collective interventions. UvA develops dedicated spatial-planning theories and urban interventions; UCR centres sustainability governance and policy advice.
Both use ArcGIS Pro and spatial data/models to create and analyse maps. UvA also introduces social-scientific research philosophy and ethics; UCR adds environmental remote sensing.

Both formulate questions and conduct collaborative applied research with external stakeholders. UvA specifically develops a regional urban vision and stakeholder roles; UCR projects concern a partner-defined sustainability problem and do not guarantee a planning studio.

Both connect research questions, theory, evidence, methods and ethical reflection in a research/policy design. UvA specifically prepares the individual geography/planning thesis; UCR produces interdisciplinary conflict-policy research and a brief.
Both study social relations, institutions and inequality. UvA specifically organises these around place, space, scales and geographical traditions; UCR supplies general sociological frameworks.
Both develop interviews, observation, qualitative research design, coding and thematic interpretation. UvA additionally integrates GIS and multivariable quantitative analysis.
Related knowledge appears in selected courses, but no additional course is counted as this dedicated geography/planning component.
Property, institutions and economic policy contribute relevant foundations, but there is no dedicated property-led urban-development course.
No selected course centres real-estate development feasibility, residual land value and urban redevelopment negotiation.
No selected course guarantees supervised research with an overseas field visit and its specific cross-context reflection.
Related knowledge appears in selected courses, but no additional course is counted as this dedicated geography/planning component.
No selected course centres the dedicated transport, accessibility and urban-mobility sequence.
The external thirty-credit elective space remains genuinely open within university-level, enrolment and approval rules.
The individual original geography/planning thesis remains compulsory. Optional UCR independent research is additional to scheduled 180 credits.

analysis: Three academic concepts are defensible: people/place/sustainability joins sociological and institutional inquiry to actual delta water governance, climate and GIS; public governance examines inequality, collective choices, law/property and policy implementation; global connections examines identity/place through imperial, Indigenous, racial, cultural and international institutional histories and social theory. These are substantial LAS responses with explicit dedicated geography/planning gaps, not merely coherent unrelated breadth.

All thirty-nine selected course contributions were reviewed from current profiles or available descriptions. Description-only social movements, climate communication, Earth System Science Tools, econometrics, Public Policy Analysis, current American Century research and Mediterranean art connections receive their actual supported scope. Econometrics supplies regression/IV/Stata and an empirical paper, not a proxy for the philosophical/research-design Methods 3 course. Earth Observation directly supplies ArcGIS Pro spatial models, vector/raster and remote-sensing methods. Earth System Tools supports climate/proxy modelling, not invented urban statistics.

Four purposeful substitutions: Sustainability Essentials II and R3 laboratory/materials courses become Public Policy Analysis and Public Economics in the closest; consumer-product design becomes Public Economics in the public option; youth-extremism educational prevention becomes general Social Psychology in the global option. Their actual content, not titles, motivates the repairs. Private Law offers comparative property/tort/contract, not a documented tenancy course. Psychological safety/inclusion and survey research in Leading Under Pressure have specific institutional/identity roles.

Partner-based Sustainable Delta research has no formal prerequisite but is only planned in 2026h2. It therefore appears in year one; the available evidence does not warrant an invented later offering or extra prerequisite. Its partner-defined investigation is not guaranteed urban studio or specified field technique. Mathematics/physical science are limited to foundations needed for environmental evidence, not equivalent human geography. Other social/political foundations are sequenced before advanced theory where feasible.

Six original offering conflicts are repaired. All plans have 24 unique courses/four per actual covered semester, 180 EC, first-year PPD and at least six advanced courses, with formal prerequisites earlier. Pairwise differences 67.5, 82.5 and 52.5 EC each way change real academic priorities, passing numerical and qualitative distinctness.

Ten bounded relationships and eight dedicated gaps account for all eighteen external components and thirty-nine selected UCR codes once. Blanket sufficiently-direct-one-to-one exclusions are removed; the standard is supported partial correspondence. Delta water inquiry provides an actual place/environment/institution strand of Urban Dynamics; ArcGIS methods relate to Thinking Spatially; qualitative coding relates to Methods 2; partner research relates to the Regional applied-project function with explicit urban-studio limits. Supervised original survey research in Leading Under Pressure relates to the Netherlands project’s quantitative strand but lacks its residential spatial/interview component. Conflict-policy research/design relates to Methods 3 with an explicit thesis-method purpose difference. Overseas fieldwork, property development, specialised mobility and individual thesis gaps remain. Optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 credits.
